results.question: According to clause 4.5.1, when does a UE NOT operating as an IAB-node perform access control checks for 5GS access?

options.A: Only when transitioning from 5GMM-IDLE mode to 5GMM-CONNECTED mode
options.B: Only for access attempts defined by the specific list of events in the clause
options.C: Only when operating in SNPN access mode
options.D: Only when the UE receives an MO-MMTEL-voice-call-started indication

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.5.1, General
results.evidence: For a UE which does not operate as an IAB-node, access control checks are performed by the UE for the 5GS access category with which the UE actions are associated, and it is performed at the point when the UE requests establishment of a NAS signalling connection or when the UE has an established NAS signalling connection and requests to send an uplink NAS message or user data over the NAS signalling connection, whichever occurs first.

results.question: For a UE operating as an IAB-node in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode with RRC inactive indication, what does the NAS provide to lower layers for access attempts identified by lower layers?

options.A: The access category and one or more access identities
options.B: Only the RRC establishment cause
options.C: The applicable access identities
options.D: Nothing, as the IAB-node skips all procedures with lower layers

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.5.1, General
results.evidence: For a UE operating as an IAB-node, when in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode with RRC inactive indication, the NAS provides an indication to the lower layers that the UE is an IAB-node for access attempts identified by lower layers, so that the lower layers can handle the access attempt accordingly (e.g. for access control purposes).

results.question: When determining the applicable access category from standardized and operator-defined categories, which subclause and table does a UE NOT operating in SNPN access mode follow?

options.A: Subclause 4.5.2 and table 4.5.2.1
options.B: Subclause 4.5.2A and table 4.5.2A.2
options.C: Subclause 4.5.2 and table 4.5.2.2
options.D: Subclause 4.5.2A and table 4.5.2A.1

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.5.1, General
results.evidence: The UE shall determine the applicable access categories, from among the standardized access categories and the operator-defined access categories, for the current access attempt as follows: a) if the UE is not operating in SNPN access mode, the UE follows subclause 6.1.3.2 of 3GPP TS 24.501 and Table 6.1.3.2.1 for the mapping of standardized access categories; and b) if the UE is operating in SNPN access mode, the UE follows subclause 6.1.3.2A and the applicable table for SNPN access category mapping.

results.question: What is specified about how and when the NAS provides applicable access identities to lower layers for access attempts in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode with RRC inactive indication?

options.A: It must be done immediately upon receiving any upper layer indication
options.B: It is specified in table 4.5.2.1
options.C: It is UE implementation specific
options.D: It is only required for IAB-node operation

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.5.1, General
results.evidence: Upon transitioning to 5GMM-CONNECTED mode with RRC inactive indication, or when a new access attempt occurs while in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode with RRC inactive indication, the NAS shall provide the applicable access identities and the establishment cause to the lower layers, so that the lower layers can determine whether access control applies before resuming the RRC connection.

results.question: Under what condition may the SMF include the IP header compression configuration IE according to clause 8.3.2.17?

options.A: When the network accepts an IP PDU session type, control plane CIoT 5GS optimization is selected, and the UE provided the IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST
options.B: When the network accepts any PDU session type and the UE supports header compression
options.C: When control plane CIoT 5GS optimization is selected, regardless of UE provisioning
options.D: When the UE provided the IE in any NAS message and an IP PDU session is established

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.1.4.1, Coordination between 5GSM and ESM with N26 interface
results.evidence: The SMF may include the IP header compression configuration IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT message only if the PDU session is a non-emergency PDU session for which control plane CIoT 5GS optimization applies, and the UE included the IP header compression configuration IE with the desired ROHC profiles in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message, and the network supports and decides to use IP header compression for that PDU session (see 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 8.3.2.17).

results.question: Which of the following is NOT a required condition for the SMF to include the IP header compression configuration IE per clause 8.3.2.17?

options.A: The network accepts an IP PDU session type
options.B: Control plane CIoT 5GS optimization is selected
options.C: The UE provided the IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message
options.D: The UE is in CM-CONNECTED state

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.1.4.1, Coordination between 5GSM and ESM with N26 interface
results.evidence: The SMF shall include the IP header compression configuration IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT message only if: a) the UE included the IP header compression configuration IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message; b) the PDU session is associated with control plane CIoT 5GS optimization; and c) the requested PDU session type is IP (i.e. IPv4, IPv6, or IPv4v6). The condition that the UE supports user plane CIoT 5GS optimization is NOT required for the SMF to include this IE, as IP header compression configuration per clause 8.3.2.17 applies specifically to control plane CIoT 5GS optimization, not user plane CIoT 5GS optimization.

results.question: According to clause 8.3.2.17, the SMF may include the IP header compression configuration IE when control plane CIoT 5GS optimization is selected and which other two conditions are met?

options.A: Network accepts IP PDU session type AND UE provided IE in PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST
options.B: UE is in idle mode AND network supports header compression
options.C: Network accepts non-IP PDU session type AND UE requested compression
options.D: UE provided IE in REGISTRATION REQUEST AND network policy allows compression

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.1.4.2, Coordination between 5GSM and ESM without N26 interface
results.evidence: The SMF may include the IP header compression configuration IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT message when control plane CIoT 5GS optimization is selected, the PDU session type is IPv4, IPv6, or IPv4v6, and the UE included the IP header compression configuration IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message indicating support for header compression.

results.question: In which specific message must the UE have provided the IP header compression configuration IE for the SMF to potentially include it, as per clause 8.3.2.17?

options.A: PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message
options.B: PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message
options.C: REGISTRATION REQUEST message
options.D: SERVICE REQUEST message

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.16, Handling of header compression for control plane CIoT optimizations
results.evidence: The SMF shall not include this IE if the IP header compression configuration IE was not provided by the UE in the PDU session establishment request message.

results.question: In the context of 5G session management states, which state is defined by the condition where no PDU session exists?

options.A: PDU SESSION ACTIVE
options.B: PDU SESSION MODIFICATION PENDING
options.C: PDU SESSION INACTIVE
options.D: PDU SESSION RELEASE REQUESTED

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.5, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: PDU SESSION INACTIVE: No PDU session exists, i.e. no PDU session context exists on the network side, or the PDU session context on the network side is in state PDU SESSION INACTIVE.

results.question: Under what condition may the UE radio capability ID information element be included in a message?

options.A: When the UE is in NB-N1 mode and the network supports RACS
options.B: When the UE is not in NB-N1 mode, both UE and network support RACS, and the network needs to assign a network-assigned UE radio capability ID
options.C: When the UE supports RACS regardless of the network's capability
options.D: When the network needs to assign a UE radio capability ID, regardless of the UE's mode

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.21, UE radio capability ID
results.evidence: The UE radio capability ID IE may be included in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message if the AMF wants to assign, update, or delete a UE radio capability ID for the UE, or if the network supports the UE radio capability ID functionality and decides to provide such an ID to the UE for storage and future use in place of full UE radio capability information.

results.question: Which of the following is NOT a required condition for including the UE radio capability ID IE according to clause 8.2.19.21?

options.A: The UE is not in NB-N1 mode
options.B: Both the UE and the network support RACS
options.C: The network needs to assign a network-assigned UE radio capability ID
options.D: The UE is in connected mode

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.21, UE radio capability ID
results.evidence: According to 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 8.2.19.21 (UE radio capability ID IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message), the AMF includes the UE radio capability ID IE only when: (a) the UE included the UE radio capability ID IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message requesting assignment/update of a UE radio capability ID (i.e. the UE radio capability ID deletion indication was not set to request deletion), (b) the AMF supports the network-assigned UE radio capability ID functionality, and (c) the AMF has successfully assigned, retrieved, or updated a UE radio capability ID for the UE. The requirement that 'the UE has changed its registered PLMN' is NOT a required condition for including this IE — a PLMN change alone does not trigger inclusion of the UE radio capability ID IE; it is only included based on the UE's request and the AMF's ability to provide/update the ID.

results.question: What must be true about RACS support for the UE radio capability ID IE to be included?

options.A: Only the UE must support RACS
options.B: Only the network must support RACS
options.C: Both the UE and the network must support RACS
options.D: RACS support is not required

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.21, UE radio capability ID
results.evidence: The network shall include the UE radio capability ID IE only if the UE supports RACS.

results.question: According to TS 24.501 Clause 5.4.1.2.2.5, when the AAA server of the CH or DCS acts as the EAP-AKA' server and successfully processes the EAP-response/AKA'-challenge, what key does it generate?

options.A: EMSK
options.B: MSK
options.C: KAUSF
options.D: KSEAF

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.5, Network successfully authenticates UE
results.evidence: When the AAA server of the CH or DCS acts as the EAP-AKA' server and it receives the EAP-response/AKA'-challenge message and processes it successfully, the AAA server generates the Master Session Key (MSK) as specified in IETF RFC 5448.

results.question: Under what condition does the AUSF or AAA server send an EAP-success message immediately after successful EAP-response/AKA'-challenge processing, according to TS 24.501 Clause 5.4.1.2.2.5?

options.A: When AT_RESULT_IND was included in the request but is missing from the response
options.B: When AT_RESULT_IND was included in both request and response
options.C: When AT_RESULT_IND was not included in the request but is present in the response
options.D: When AT_RESULT_IND was included in the response but not in the request

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.5, Network successfully authenticates UE
results.evidence: If the AUSF or the AAA server does not need to send additional EAP-request messages to the UE (i.e. if the EAP-response/AKA'-challenge message is successfully processed and no further EAP method messages are needed), the AUSF or the AAA server sends an EAP-success message immediately after receiving and successfully processing the EAP-response/AKA'-challenge message.

results.question: When the AUSF acts as the EAP-AKA' server and successfully processes the EAP-response/AKA'-challenge, which key does it generate directly from the EMSK according to TS 24.501 Clause 5.4.1.2.2.5?

options.A: MSK
options.B: KSEAF
options.C: KAUSF
options.D: KAMF

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.5, Network successfully authenticates UE
results.evidence: Upon successful processing of the EAP-response/AKA'-challenge message received from the UE, the AUSF acting as EAP server shall generate the anchor key (referred to as the K_AUSF, see 3GPP TS 33.501 [24]) directly from the EMSK as specified in 3GPP TS 33.501 [24].

results.question: According to NOTE 1 in TS 24.501 Clause 5.4.1.2.2.5, when the AAA server of CH/DCS acts as EAP-AKA' server, what does the AAA server provide to the AUSF via the NSSAAF?

options.A: KSEAF and SUPI
options.B: MSK and SUPI
options.C: KAUSF and KSEAF
options.D: EMSK and SUPI

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.5, Network successfully authenticates UE
results.evidence: NOTE 1: The AAA server of the CH/DCS acting as the EAP-AKA' server, provides the AUSF, via the NSSAAF, with the master session key derived from the primary authentication and key agreement procedure for SNPN with CH.

results.question: What action does the network take immediately upon receiving an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message?

options.A: It starts timer T3560
options.B: It stops timer T3560 and checks RES* correctness
options.C: It sends an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST with a new ngKSI
options.D: It renegotiates with UDM/AUSF for new parameters

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.4, Authentication completion by the network
results.evidence: Upon receipt of the AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message, the AMF shall stop timer T3560.

results.question: When initiating a new 5G AKA based primary authentication procedure after successful completion, what must the network include in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message?

options.A: The same ngKSI value stored in the 5G NAS security context
options.B: A different ngKSI value than previously used
options.C: 5GMM cause #21 'synch failure'
options.D: No ngKSI value is required

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.4, Authentication completion by the network
results.evidence: If the network initiates a new authentication procedure with 5G AKA after a previous authentication procedure with 5G AKA was completed successfully, then the network shall include a new value for ngKSI in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message and this value shall differ from the value that was assigned in the previous authentication procedure.

results.question: What network action is triggered upon receiving an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message with 5GMM cause #21 'synch failure'?

options.A: The network stops timer T3560 and must renegotiate with UDM/AUSF
options.B: The network stops timer T3560 and may renegotiate with UDM/AUSF
options.C: The network continues timer T3560 and resends the same authentication parameters
options.D: The network immediately terminates the authentication procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.4, Authentication completion by the network
results.evidence: Upon receipt of an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message with the 5GMM cause value #21 "synch failure", the AMF shall send an authentication information request to the AUSF with a "synchronization failure indication" in order to obtain new authentication vectors for the UE.

results.question: Under what condition does the network include a different ngKSI value in a new AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message?

options.A: When any AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message is received
options.B: When timer T3560 expires without response
options.C: When 5G AKA authentication completes successfully and ngKSI is stored in the security context
options.D: When the network receives an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE with incorrect RES*

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.4, Authentication completion by the network
results.evidence: If the network wants to proceed with an authentication procedure, it needs to select an ngKSI value different from the previous ones. If a new AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message is sent to the UE due to a failed integrity check, the network shall set the ngKSI to the value that was included in the previous AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message; otherwise, the network shall include a different ngKSI value in a new AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message.

results.question: According to TS 24.501 Clause 8.2.10.9, what are the two scenarios that the Release assistance indication IE can inform the network about?

options.A: No further uplink/downlink data expected; OR only a single uplink transmission and no further downlink expected
options.B: No further uplink/downlink data expected; OR only a single downlink transmission and no further uplink expected after uplink data
options.C: Only emergency calls expected; OR only background data transmission expected
options.D: Network-initiated release required; OR UE power saving mode activation

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.10.9, Release assistance indication
results.evidence: The release assistance indication IE, if present, indicates whether the UE requests the network to release the PDU session or not, and if so, whether the release of the PDU session is intended for the case of no further uplink or downlink data transmission expected after the transmission of the request, or whether the release is intended for the case of no further uplink or downlink data transmission expected after the receipt of the response from the network. The release assistance indication informs the network about: a) the UE expects only a single downlink data transmission and no further uplink or downlink data transmission is expected after the single downlink data transmission (i.e., no further uplink or downlink data transmission is expected after the transmission of the request); or b) the UE expects only a single uplink and a single downlink data transmission and no further uplink or downlink data transmission is expected after the single uplink and downlink data transmission (i.e., no further uplink or downlink data transmission is expected after the receipt of the response from the network).

results.question: When a UE includes the Release assistance indication IE to signal that only a single downlink data transmission is expected, what type of downlink transmission might this typically represent?

options.A: A new downlink data session initiation
options.B: An acknowledgement or response to uplink data
options.C: A network paging message
options.D: A system information broadcast

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.10.9, Release assistance indication
results.evidence: The value "1" indicates that only a single downlink data transmission (and no further uplink and downlink data transmission) is expected after this uplink data transmission, e.g. the expected mobile originated data transmission is a single message and the network is not expected to provide a response.

results.question: In the context of Release assistance indication, what does the UE indicate when it expects 'no further uplink and no further downlink data transmission'?

options.A: Only downlink streaming will continue
options.B: Data transmission is complete in both directions
options.C: Uplink transmission will continue but downlink will stop
options.D: The UE is about to initiate a handover procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.10.9, Release assistance indication
results.evidence: In the Release assistance indication (RAI) information element (3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 9.11.4.2), the UE sets the RAI value to '1' to indicate 'No further uplink data transmission and no further downlink data transmission is expected after the current uplink data transmission.' This value informs the network that the current PDU session/user-plane resources can be released immediately after the uplink NAS or user-plane data transfer, as no additional uplink or downlink data is anticipated.

results.question: What is the purpose of the Release assistance indication IE as defined in TS 24.501 Clause 8.2.10.9?

options.A: To request additional network resources for high-speed data
options.B: To inform the network about expected future data transmission patterns
options.C: To report radio link failure to the network
options.D: To initiate a quality of service modification procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.10.9, Release assistance indication
results.evidence: The Release assistance indication information element is used by the UE to provide the network with information about the expected traffic behaviour on a PDU session, enabling the network to decide whether the PDU session's user-plane resources or the N1 NAS signalling connection can be released immediately after the completion of a single or a few packet transmission(s), thereby supporting efficient control of user-plane and NAS signalling connection release for optimizing UE power consumption and network resource usage (e.g., for CIoT devices with infrequent, small data transmissions).

results.question: According to TS 24.501 Clause 4.4.3.3, what does the sender use as input to the integrity protection algorithm for NAS COUNT?

options.A: The NAS sequence number from the received message
options.B: Its locally stored NAS COUNT
options.C: An estimate for the NAS overflow counter
options.D: The NAS COUNT value from the previous successful verification

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.3.3, Integrity protection and verification
results.evidence: For the purpose of NAS integrity protection, the sender uses the 24-bit NAS COUNT value applicable for the NAS message and calculates it as an input to the integrity protection algorithm as specified in subclause 4.4.3.3, where the sender constructs the NAS COUNT by concatenating the corresponding NAS sequence number with the NAS overflow counter to form a 24-bit value, which together with the 96-bit COUNT (with the 24-bit NAS COUNT stored in the least significant bits, zero padded in the most significant bits) is used as input for the integrity protection algorithm.

results.question: For integrity verification of a SECURITY PROTECTED 5GS NAS MESSAGE, which octets are included in the integrity protection calculation?

options.A: Octets 1 to 6 only
options.B: Octet 7 only
options.C: Octets 7 to n (Sequence number IE and NAS message IE)
options.D: All octets of the entire message

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.3.3, Integrity protection and verification
results.evidence: The NAS-MAC is calculated over the plain 5GS NAS message (i.e., the Sequence number octet and the Plain NAS message octet(s)) prepended with the 5G NAS security context specific input parameters (COUNT, direction bit, bearer identity) as specified in 3GPP TS 33.501, and the resulting NAS-MAC is included in the Message authentication code octets of the SECURITY PROTECTED NAS MESSAGE. For the purpose of integrity protection verification, the integrity protection is calculated over the Sequence number octet and the Plain NAS message octets, i.e., octets 5 to n of the SECURITY PROTECTED NAS MESSAGE, and shall not include the Extended protocol discriminator, Security header type, and the Message authentication code octets themselves.

results.question: What action must the receiver take after successful integrity protection validation of a NAS message?

options.A: Discard the locally stored NAS COUNT
options.B: Update its locally stored NAS COUNT with the estimated NAS COUNT for this message
options.C: Reset the NAS COUNT to zero
options.D: Forward the NAS COUNT to the sender for confirmation

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.3.3, Integrity protection and verification
results.evidence: Upon successful integrity protection validation of a NAS message, the receiving NAS entity shall consider the message as integrity protected and authentic, and shall proceed to process the message as specified for that message type. The receiver shall also update the stored NAS COUNT value for the corresponding direction (uplink or downlink) to the value used in the successfully verified message, provided that this NAS COUNT value is greater than the previously stored NAS COUNT value for that direction.

results.question: Which of the following statements about integrity verification is correct according to TS 24.501 Clause 4.4.3.3?

options.A: Integrity verification is always required for all NAS messages
options.B: Integrity verification is not applicable when 5G-IA0 is used
options.C: Integrity verification uses only the NAS sequence number as input
options.D: Integrity verification includes octets 1-6 of the NAS transparent container

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.3.3, Integrity protection and verification
results.evidence: Once a security context exists and has been taken into use, all NAS signalling messages exchanged between the UE and the AMF shall be integrity protected, except for the specific NAS messages listed as exceptions (e.g. IDENTITY REQUEST/RESPONSE requesting/containing SUCI, AUTHENTICATION REQUEST/REJECT, SECURITY MODE COMMAND/REJECT sent before security context activation, DEREGISTRATION REQUEST/ACCEPT for non-3GPP access when no valid security context exists). The UE and the AMF shall discard NAS messages, other than these exceptions, that fail integrity check or are received without integrity protection while a security context is established.

results.question: Based on TS 24.501 Clause 6.2.3, which entity is responsible for transferring the session management messages between the UE and the SMF?

options.A: UPF
options.B: PCF
options.C: AMF
options.D: NEF

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.3, PDU session management
results.evidence: The AMF is responsible for transferring the session management (SM) messages between the UE and the SMF as specified in TS 24.501 Clause 6.2.3, acting as a transparent relay that forwards N1 SM signalling using the NAS transport procedure without interpreting the SM message content.

results.question: As per TS 24.501 Clause 6.2.3, a UE may establish multiple PDU sessions. Which of the following statements about this capability is TRUE?

options.A: Multiple PDU sessions can only be established to different data networks.
options.B: Multiple PDU sessions can be established via 3GPP and Non-3GPP access networks simultaneously.
options.C: Multiple PDU sessions must all use the same type of access network.
options.D: A UE is limited to a maximum of two concurrent PDU sessions.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.3, PDU session management
results.evidence: The UE can determine that two PDU sessions are associated with each other, if both PDU sessions have the same PDU session address lifetime, DNN, and S-NSSAI, but different SSC modes or different PDU session types.

results.question: According to the responsibilities of the SMF outlined in TS 24.501 Clause 6.2.3, which procedure is specifically initiated by the network for modifying a PDU session?

options.A: UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure
options.B: UE-requested PDU session modification procedure
options.C: Network-requested PDU session modification procedure
options.D: PDU session authentication and authorization procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.3, PDU session management
results.evidence: The SMF also handles the network-requested PDU session modification procedure, which allows the network to initiate a modification of an established PDU session in order to change its QoS parameters, network slice information, or other session attributes without requiring the UE to request such changes.

results.question: Under what condition does a MUSIM UE indicate support for the paging restriction feature during registration?

options.A: If the UE supports any MUSIM feature and the network indicates acceptance
options.B: If the UE has indicated support for N1 NAS signalling connection release or reject paging request (or both) and supports paging restriction
options.C: If the UE is operating in NB-N1 mode or WB-N1 mode CE mode B
options.D: If the network indicates support for paging restriction first during registration

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.25, Support of MUSIM features
results.evidence: If the UE supports the paging restriction feature, the UE shall indicate support for this feature only if it also supports the MUSIM feature, by setting the PR (Paging Restriction) bit to '1' in the 5GMM Capability IE of the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.

results.question: When does the network NOT indicate support for any MUSIM feature to the UE during registration?

options.A: When the UE is operating in NB-N1 mode
options.B: During the registration for emergency services
options.C: When the UE does not support paging timing collision control
options.D: When the UE has stopped fulfilling MUSIM UE conditions

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.25, Support of MUSIM features
results.evidence: The network shall not indicate support for any MUSIM feature to the UE, if the UE has not indicated support for the MUSIM feature in the 5GMM capability IE of the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.

results.question: What action must a UE take if it stops fulfilling the conditions to be considered a MUSIM UE and has previously negotiated support for MUSIM features?

options.A: Immediately release all NAS signalling connections
options.B: Initiate a registration procedure to indicate that all MUSIM features are not supported (except paging timing collision control)
options.C: Continue using previously negotiated features until network reconfiguration
options.D: Send a reject paging request to the network

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.25, Support of MUSIM features
results.evidence: If the UE stops fulfilling the conditions to be considered a MUSIM UE (see subclause 4.23.1) after having negotiated support for MUSIM features with the network, the UE shall locally disable the use of the negotiated MUSIM features and, if needed, shall initiate a registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update in order to indicate to the network, via the 5GMM capability IE, that it no longer supports MUSIM signalling connection related functionality.

results.question: In which operational mode does a MUSIM UE NOT indicate support for paging indication for voice services during registration?

options.A: When operating in single-SIM mode
options.B: When the network has not indicated support for any MUSIM features
options.C: When operating in NB-N1 mode or in WB-N1 mode CE mode B
options.D: During initial registration after power-on

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.25, Support of MUSIM features
results.evidence: A MUSIM UE shall not indicate support for paging indication for voice services in the 5GS registration request message when performing an initial registration for emergency services (i.e. registering over a PLMN for emergency services only or performing an emergency registration).

results.question: What does the Allowed PDU session status IE indicate when included in a SERVICE REQUEST message sent as a response to paging/notification via 3GPP access?

options.A: The list of PDU sessions to be deactivated
options.B: The user-plane resources of PDU sessions associated with non-3GPP access allowed for re-establishment over 3GPP access
options.C: The preferred access type for all PDU sessions
options.D: The QoS parameters for new PDU sessions

results.evidence: As specified in 3GPP TS 24.501 Clause 4.8.3, a UE operating in dual-registration mode can be simultaneously registered with 5GC over one access network (e.g., 3GPP access) and with EPC over another access network (e.g., non-3GPP access or a different RAT), maintaining two independent registrations with separate GUTIs, security contexts, and mobility management states. results.question: According to TS 24.501 clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, what action does the AMF take upon the fifth expiry of timer T3560 during an EAP-based primary authentication procedure?

options.A: Retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message and restart timer T3560.
options.B: Abort the EAP-based primary authentication and key agreement procedure, abort any ongoing 5GMM specific procedure, and release the N1 NAS signalling connection.
options.C: Initiate a fallback to non-EAP authentication and restart the procedure.
options.D: Wait for lower layers to indicate handover completion before taking any action.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: On the fifth expiry of timer T3560, the AMF shall abort the authentication procedure, release the established NAS signalling connection, and if any, release the existing EPS NAS signalling connection.

results.question: In the abnormal case where an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message cannot be delivered due to an intra-AMF handover, under what condition should the AMF retransmit the message upon successful handover completion?

options.A: Always, regardless of the target Tracking Area.
options.B: Only if the handover failure is reported by the lower layers.
options.C: Only if the target Tracking Area is included in the TAI list.
options.D: Only if timer T3560 has not yet expired.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: If the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message cannot be delivered due to an intra-AMF handover, then upon successful completion of the intra-AMF handover, the network shall retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message if no NAS signalling connection recovery procedure is triggered.

results.question: What is the specified AMF behavior following the FIRST expiry of timer T3560 during the EAP-based primary authentication procedure?

options.A: Abort the authentication procedure immediately.
options.B: Retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message, reset and start timer T3560.
options.C: Wait for a lower layer handover indication before proceeding.
options.D: Switch to an alternative authentication method.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: Upon the first expiry of the timer T3560, the AMF shall retransmit the SECURITY MODE COMMAND message and shall reset and restart timer T3560. This retransmission is repeated four times, i.e. on the fifth expiry of timer T3560, the AMF shall abort the procedure and release the NAS signalling connection.

results.question: According to the abnormal cases for non-delivered NAS PDU, when should the AMF retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message if a failure of the handover procedure is reported by the lower layer?

options.A: Only if the target TA is in the TAI list and timer T3560 is still running.
options.B: Only if the N1 NAS signalling connection no longer exists.

options.D: If the N1 NAS signalling connection exists.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: If a NAS signalling connection exists and if a failure of the handover procedure is reported by the lower layer after the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message was submitted to the lower layer and before the AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message is received, the AMF shall retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message, if the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message has not been retransmitted four times.

results.question: According to TS 24.501 Clause 7.6.1, how should a UE handle an Information Element (IE) in a received message that is unknown and encoded as 'comprehension required'?

options.A: Ignore the IE completely
options.B: Reject the entire message
options.C: Process the IE according to its best interpretation
options.D: The clause does not specify behavior for 'comprehension required' IEs

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 7.6.1, IEIs unknown in the message
results.evidence: If an information element with format 'comprehension required' is defined as an unknown IE (i.e. an IE not defined, or defined as spare, in the version of the protocol supported by the receiver) in a message, the UE shall treat the message as if the message contained an IE with 'comprehension required' error according to subclause 7.7.

results.question: What action does TS 24.501 Clause 7.6.1 mandate for both the UE and network regarding unknown IEs that are NOT encoded as 'comprehension required'?

options.A: Reject the message containing them
options.B: Ignore them
options.C: Store them for future reference
options.D: Respond with an error indication

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 7.6.1, IEIs unknown in the message
results.evidence: If the UE or network receives an information element defined as an unknown, but syntactically correct, non-comprehension required IE, it shall ignore this information element and shall process the rest of the message as if this information element was absent, except that the UE or network shall consider that the message contains the information element for the purpose of the abnormal cases described in the present document.

results.question: Based on TS 24.501 Clause 7.6.1, which entity is explicitly stated to follow the same approach as the UE regarding handling of unknown IEs?

options.A: The serving gateway (SGW)
options.B: The packet data network gateway (PGW)
options.C: The network
options.D: The home subscriber server (HSS)

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 7.6.1, IEIs unknown in the message
results.evidence: If the AMF receives an information element with a value that is not in the range of values defined for that information element, it shall follow the same approach as the UE, i.e., treat the information element as if it were absent from the message and, if the corresponding message description in clause 8 indicates that the information element is mandatory, follow the applicable message handling procedure specified in the present subclause.

results.question: Which 3GPP TS 24.501 clause specifies the inclusion condition for the EAP message IE in a SERVICE REJECT message?

options.A: Clause 8.2.18.1
options.B: Clause 8.2.18.2
options.C: Clause 8.2.18.3
options.D: Clause 8.2.18.4

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.18.4, EAP message
results.evidence: Clause 8.2.25 (SERVICE REJECT) of 3GPP TS 24.501 specifies, in the message definition table, that the EAP message IE is included only when the 5GMM cause value indicates that the network rejects the service request due to a failure in EAP-based authentication procedure (i.e., the EAP message IE is present when EAP-based primary authentication has failed and the network wants to send the EAP-failure message to the UE within the SERVICE REJECT message).

results.question: According to 3GPP TS 24.501 Clause 5.3.1, which of the following correctly describes the 5GMM mode of operation when the UE is in CM-IDLE state and has no N1 NAS signalling connection established?

options.A: 5GMM-IDLE mode
options.B: 5GMM-CONNECTED mode
options.C: 5GMM-REGISTERED mode
options.D: 5GMM-DEREGISTERED mode

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.1, 5GMM modes and N1 NAS signalling connection
results.evidence: As specified in 3GPP TS 24.501 Clause 5.3.1, two 5GMM modes are defined for the UE: 5GMM-IDLE mode and 5GMM-CONNECTED mode. The UE is in 5GMM-IDLE mode when it is in CM-IDLE state, i.e., when no N1 NAS signalling connection exists between the UE and the AMF. In this mode, the UE performs cell selection/reselection and PLMN selection, and no NAS signalling connection is established over N1. The UE enters 5GMM-CONNECTED mode only when an N1 NAS signalling connection is established between the UE and the AMF; otherwise, it remains in 5GMM-IDLE mode.

results.question: Which of the following statements about the relationship between 5GMM modes and N1 NAS signalling connection is FALSE based on Clause 5.3.1?

options.A: A UE in 5GMM-IDLE mode has no N1 NAS signalling connection established
options.B: The establishment of an N1 NAS signalling connection causes a transition from 5GMM-IDLE to 5GMM-CONNECTED mode
options.C: A UE can be in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode without an N1 NAS signalling connection
options.D: The release of the N1 NAS signalling connection causes a transition from 5GMM-CONNECTED to 5GMM-IDLE mode

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.1, 5GMM modes and N1 NAS signalling connection
results.evidence: The two 5GMM modes, 5GMM-IDLE mode and 5GMM-CONNECTED mode, describe the different states of the UE from an NAS perspective. In 5GMM-IDLE mode, there is no N1 NAS signalling connection between the UE and the network, whereas in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode, an N1 NAS signalling connection exists between the UE and the network. Therefore, a statement claiming that a UE can be in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode without an N1 NAS signalling connection established between the UE and the AMF is FALSE.

results.question: What triggers the transition of a UE from 5GMM-CONNECTED mode to 5GMM-IDLE mode according to Clause 5.3.1?

options.A: When the UE moves out of coverage of the registered PLMN
options.B: When the UE's registration timer expires
options.C: When the N1 NAS signalling connection is released
options.D: When the UE initiates a service request procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.1, 5GMM modes and N1 NAS signalling connection
results.evidence: The UE enters 5GMM-CONNECTED mode over the 3GPP access when the RRC connection is established over the 3GPP access. The UE enters 5GMM-IDLE mode over the 3GPP access when the RRC connection is released or the RRC connection establishment fails.

results.question: According to TS 24.501 Clause 6.3.2.1, which of the following is NOT a stated purpose of the network-requested PDU session modification procedure?

options.A: To re-negotiate header compression configuration associated to a PDU session
options.B: To provide updated DNS server address(es) due to the newly selected local DNS server
options.C: To establish a new PDU session for a different Data Network Name (DNN)
options.D: To update the MBS service area of an MBS multicast session that the UE has joined

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.1, General
results.evidence: The purpose of the network-requested PDU session modification procedure is to enable the network to update, add or delete QoS flow(s) or QoS rule(s) of a PDU session or to update the PDU session by adding or deleting a small data rate control status, serving PLMN rate control status, or an APN rate control status; and this procedure is used by the network to modify PDU session with 5GSM congestion re-attempt indicator or to change the extended protocol configuration options. The network-requested PDU session modification procedure is not used to release a PDU session (the PDU session release procedure is used for that purpose).

results.question: Based on TS 24.501 Clause 6.3.2.1, the network-requested PDU session modification procedure can be used to inform the UE about the result of which specific procedure for UAS services?

options.A: The result of the PDU session establishment procedure
options.B: The result of service-level AA procedure or C2 authorization
options.C: The result of the UE policy delivery procedure
options.D: The result of the UE configuration update procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.1, General
results.evidence: The network may also use the network-requested PDU session modification procedure to inform the UE about the result of the aerial UE subscription information update procedure for the purpose of using UAS services, as specified in subclause 6.3.2 of 3GPP TS 24.501.

results.question: According to the general description in TS 24.501 Clause 6.3.2.1, the network-requested PDU session modification procedure can be used to provide updated ECS configuration information and to perform which other specific update related to traffic steering?

options.A: Update the UE's allowed NSSAI
options.B: Update ATSSS parameters (e.g. ATSSS rules)
options.C: Update the UE's Route Selection Policy (URSP) rules
options.D: Update the network slice selection policy

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.1, General
results.evidence: The network-requested PDU session modification procedure can be used by the network to update ECS (Edge Configuration Server) configuration information provided to the UE, and to update information used by the UE for EAS (Edge Application Server) rediscovery, e.g. to trigger the UE to perform traffic steering to a different EAS or to update the target DNAI(s) and corresponding traffic descriptors for the PDU session.

results.question: According to TS 24.501 Clause 6.3.1A, what is the primary purpose of the service-level authentication and authorization (service-level-AA) procedure?

options.A: To authenticate the upper layers of the UE when establishing the PDU session
options.B: To authorize the upper layers of the UE when establishing the PDU session
options.C: Both to authenticate and authorize the upper layers of the UE when establishing the PDU session
options.D: To re-authenticate the upper layers of the UE after establishment of the PDU session

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1A, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure
results.evidence: The service-level-AA procedure over the user plane is used between the UE and the AF for the service-level device authentication or between the UE and the AF for the service-level authentication for a service enabler, as specified in 3GPP TS 33.501. The purpose of the service-level-AA procedure is to authenticate and authorize the UE for a specific service, e.g. for the use of a 5G LAN-virtual network or a service enabler, based on the service-level-AA container information transferred between the UE and the network.

results.question: During which type of PDU session establishment procedure is the service-level authentication and authorization procedure explicitly prohibited?

options.A: A non-emergency PDU session
options.B: An emergency PDU session
options.C: A network-requested PDU session
options.D: A UE-requested PDU session with re-authentication

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1A, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure
results.evidence: The SMF shall not initiate a service-level authentication and authorization procedure for a PDU session established for emergency services (i.e. a PDU session with the request type set to 'emergency request' or 'existing emergency PDU session').

results.question: If the service-level-AA procedure is performed for an established PDU session with re-authentication purpose and completes unsuccessfully, how is the service-level-AA response transported from the network to the UE?

options.A: As part of the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT message
options.B: As part of the network-requested PDU session modification procedure in the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message
options.C: As part of the network-requested PDU session release procedure in the PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND message
options.D: As part of the UE-requested PDU session modification procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1A, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure
results.evidence: The network shall use the DL NAS TRANSPORT message to transport the service-level-AA response message and other service-level-AA parameter(s), if any, to the UE, when a service-level-AA procedure is performed for an established PDU session for the purpose of re-authentication and the service-level-AA procedure completes unsuccessfully.

results.question: What does the UE do if it receives the service-level-AA response in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT or PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT message?

options.A: It discards the response as the procedure is complete
options.B: It initiates a new service-level-AA procedure
options.C: It passes the response to the upper layer
options.D: It stores the response for future re-authentication

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1A, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure
results.evidence: Upon receipt of a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT message or a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT message containing a Service-level-AA container IE with a service-level-AA response, the UE shall forward the service-level-AA response, together with any service-level device ID, service-level-AA payload, and (if included) the service-level-AA payload type, to the upper layers for further action. The upper layers determine whether the service-level authentication and authorization was successful or not, based on the content of the service-level-AA response, and take appropriate action (e.g. use of the PDU session for the associated service, or release of the PDU session if authorization failed).

results.question: Under what condition is the EAP message information element included according to TS 24.501 clause 8.3.2.8?

options.A: When the UE initiates an EAP authentication procedure
options.B: When the external DN successfully performed authentication and authorization of the UE using EAP
options.C: When the network requires EAP-based re-authentication
options.D: When the UE supports EAP-AKA' authentication method

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.2.8, EAP message

results.question: According to clause 8.3.2.8, the EAP message IE is included specifically when:

options.A: The UE requests EAP-based service authorization
options.B: The serving PLMN performs EAP authentication
options.C: External DN successfully authenticates and authorizes UE using EAP
options.D: The UE provides EAP credentials during registration

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.2.8, EAP message
results.evidence: The EAP message IE is included in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message if the type of authentication procedure that is used for primary authentication and key agreement is based on EAP, i.e., when EAP is used as the authentication method.

results.question: According to TS 24.501 Clause 6.2.5.1.1.1, in which PDU session type(s) does the NAS protocol enable different forwarding treatments of UL user data packets based on QoS rules?

options.A: Only IPv4 and IPv6 PDU session types
options.B: IPv4, IPv6, IPv4v6, and Ethernet PDU session types
options.C: All PDU session types including Unstructured
options.D: Only Unstructured PDU session type

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.1.1, General
results.evidence: The NAS protocol enables different forwarding treatment of uplink (UL) user data packets based on QoS rules for PDU sessions of type "IP" and PDU sessions of type "Ethernet".

results.question: For a PDU session of Unstructured type, how are all UL user data packets handled with respect to QoS flows?

options.A: They are distributed across multiple QoS flows based on packet size
options.B: They are associated with different QoS flows according to signalled rules
options.C: They are all associated with the same QoS flow
options.D: They bypass QoS flow association entirely

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.1.1, General
results.evidence: For a PDU session of Unstructured type, all the UL user data received from the upper layers shall be associated with the QoS flow which is used to carry signalling as specified in subclause 6.2.2, i.e. the default QoS rule of the PDU session, unless explicit port management information container is used to bind the traffic to a specific QoS flow.

results.question: In the specified clause, what is the basis for enabling different forwarding treatments of UL user data packets in applicable PDU session types?

options.A: Only signalled QoS rules
options.B: Only derived QoS rules
options.C: Signalled QoS rules, derived QoS rules, or any combination of them
options.D: Network operator policy exclusively

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.1.1, General
results.evidence: The basis is the use of QoS rules containing packet filters whose contents (i.e., the packet filter components that can be included) are defined according to the applicable PDU session type (e.g. IPv4, IPv6, IPv4v6, Ethernet, Unstructured). Because the set of allowed packet filter components differs per PDU session type, the QoS rules can classify and enable different forwarding treatment of UL user data packets according to the PDU session type of the PDU session over which they are sent (see 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 6.1.3.2 and Annex clause 9.11.4.13 on QoS rules).

results.question: Which PDU session type is explicitly described as having all UL user data packets associated with a single QoS flow?

options.A: IPv4v6
options.B: Ethernet
options.C: Unstructured
options.D: IPv6

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.1.1, General
results.evidence: For a PDU session of Ethernet PDU session type, all UL user data packets are associated with a single QoS flow, i.e. the QoS flow associated with the default QoS rule for that PDU session.

results.question: According to TS 24.501 clause 6.4.1.2, what must a UE do when requesting to establish a new PDU session regarding the PDU session ID?

options.A: It shall allocate a PDU session ID not currently used by any other PDU session over either 3GPP or non-3GPP access.
options.B: It shall always allocate PDU session identity value 15 for new sessions.
options.C: It shall reuse an existing PDU session ID from a recently released session.
options.D: It shall let the network allocate the PDU session ID and include a request for allocation.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.2, UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure initiation
results.evidence: When the UE requests the establishment of a new PDU session, it shall select the value of the PDU session ID that is not already in use for a currently active PDU session of the UE and include it in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message.

results.question: Under what condition does a 'voice centric' UE in 5GMM-REGISTERED state receive a request from upper layers to establish a PDU session for IMS signalling?

options.A: When the UE is in idle mode and detects a new cell.
options.B: When IMS voice is available over either 3GPP or non-3GPP access and conditions for initial IMS registration are satisfied.
options.C: When the UE is performing a handover from 4G to 5G.
options.D: When the UE receives a network command for IMS emergency services.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.2, UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure initiation
results.evidence: If the UE is a 'voice centric' UE and, while in 5GMM-REGISTERED state, receives a request from upper layers to establish a PDU session for IMS signalling, and the UE has an indication that the current PLMN or the current registered area does not support voice services over NG-RAN (i.e. IMS voice over PS session is not available in 5GS, as indicated by the network via the 'IMS voice over PS session supported' indicator or absence of voice support indication in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message, or the UE is otherwise informed that 5G voice services are unavailable), the UE shall attempt to perform mobility to E-UTRAN connected to EPC (i.e. fallback to EPS) rather than establishing the PDU session for IMS signalling over 5GS, in accordance with the UE's voice centric usage setting.

results.question: What is a specific restriction regarding PDU session identity value 15 for an N5CW device establishing a new PDU session via 3GPP access?

options.A: The N5CW device must allocate PDU session identity value 15.
options.B: The N5CW device shall refrain from allocating PDU session identity value 15.
options.C: The N5CW device may allocate PDU session identity value 15 only for emergency sessions.
options.D: The N5CW device must request network permission to use PDU session identity value 15.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.2, UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure initiation
results.evidence: The UE shall not use PDU session identity value 15 for a PDU session established over 3GPP access if the UE is an N5CW device, since PDU session identity value 15 is reserved for use by the non-3GPP access (i.e., for the PDU session used to reach the trusted WLAN access network via a W-AGF or for other non-3GPP related purposes as specified). Specifically, an N5CW device shall not include PDU session identity value 15 in a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message sent over 3GPP access, as this value is reserved for the non-3GPP access PDU session context associated with the N5CW device's registration via trusted WLAN.

results.question: When the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message includes the Service-level-AA container IE and certain conditions are met, what action does the SMF take regarding the request?

options.A: The SMF shall immediately reject the request with a cause code for missing authorization.
options.B: The SMF shall proceed with the UUAA-SM procedure and refrain from accepting/rejecting until service-level authentication/authorization is completed.
options.C: The SMF shall accept the request provisionally and initiate a timer for authorization.
options.D: The SMF shall forward the request to the PCF for policy decision before any action.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.2, UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure initiation
results.evidence: If the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message includes the Service-level-AA container IE and the SMF determines that service-level authentication and authorization is required for the requested PDU session, the SMF shall not proceed with the PDU session establishment procedure until the service-level-AA procedure is completed. The SMF shall forward the service-level-AA payload contained in the Service-level-AA container IE to the service-level-AA server, and shall use the received response to determine whether to continue, modify, or reject the PDU session establishment request.

results.question: From the UE's NAS perspective, how are the procedures and messages defined for 5GMM and 5GSM generally used over non-3GPP access compared to 3GPP access?

options.A: Completely different procedures and messages are used exclusively for non-3GPP access.
options.B: They are used in the same way as over 3GPP access.
options.C: They are used with significant modifications and different message formats.
options.D: They are not supported over non-3GPP access; only 3GPP access is defined.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.7.1, General
results.evidence: Unless specified otherwise, the 5GMM procedures and 5GSM procedures described in this specification apply to both 3GPP access and non-3GPP access. Specific behaviours for non-3GPP access are indicated where the procedure differs from the one used over 3GPP access, e.g. for N1 NAS signalling connection establishment via non-3GPP access, the UE performs the registration procedure over non-3GPP access using the same message formats and information elements as defined for 3GPP access, with certain access-specific parameters (e.g. access type indication) included to distinguish between 3GPP access and non-3GPP access.

results.question: According to Clause 4.7.1, what is the general relationship between the handling of 5GMM/5GSM procedures over non-3GPP and 3GPP access?

options.A: The procedures are fundamentally incompatible between the two access types.
options.B: The same procedures and messages are generally used for both access types.
options.C: Non-3GPP access uses a simplified subset of the 3GPP access procedures.
options.D: Non-3GPP access requires entirely new NAS protocol definitions.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.7.1, General
results.evidence: Unless specified otherwise, the 5GMM and 5GSM procedures that apply for a UE connected via a 3GPP access also apply for a UE connected via a non-3GPP access.

results.question: What does Clause 4.7.1 state about potential differences in 5GMM/5GSM procedures for non-3GPP access?

options.A: There are no differences whatsoever; operation is identical.
options.B: A number of aspects are different, as described in subsequent subclauses.
options.C: Differences are only in the physical layer, not in NAS procedures.
options.D: Differences are so major that the general principle of similar usage does not apply.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.7.1, General
results.evidence: Unless explicitly stated otherwise, the 5GMM and 5GSM procedures specified in the present document for 3GPP access are also applicable for non-3GPP access. However, certain 5GMM and 5GSM procedures, or parts thereof, are applicable only for 3GPP access or only for non-3GPP access, as indicated in the relevant procedure description.

results.question: What type of information does the Extended protocol configuration options IE enable the network to transmit to the UE, as specified in TS 24.501 Clause 8.3.2.10?

options.A: Only authentication vectors and security keys
options.B: Exclusively mobility management timers
options.C: Protocol data such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events
options.D: Serving cell measurement reports and neighbor lists

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.2.10, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The Extended protocol configuration options IE is used to transfer external network protocol options associated with a PDU session establishment and additional parameters, and to enable the transfer of information that is not specific to any particular PDP type or PDU session type, such as configuration parameters, error codes, or other information from the network to the UE, e.g. for further processing by a layer above NAS (e.g. DNS server addresses, P-CSCF addresses, DHCP related parameters, and other similar information relevant to upper layers).

results.question: According to clause 7.5, what is the UE's required action when it receives a 5GMM message containing a mandatory information element with a syntactically correct but semantically incorrect value?

options.A: Ignore the information element and process the rest of the message normally
options.B: Treat the entire message as containing a protocol error and initiate appropriate error handling
options.C: Process the message using the semantically incorrect value as received
options.D: Discard the entire message and send an error indication to the network

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 7.5, Non-semantical mandatory information element errors

results.question: What is the specified UE behavior when a syntactically incorrect mandatory information element is received in a 5GMM message, according to clause 7.5?

options.A: Process the message using a default value for that information element
options.B: Treat the message as containing a protocol error and act accordingly
options.C: Ignore that specific information element but process the rest of the message
options.D: Attempt to correct the syntax error before processing

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 7.5, Non-semantical mandatory information element errors
results.evidence: According to 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 7.5 (Handling of unknown, unforeseen, and erroneous protocol data), if a 5GMM message is received containing an information element that is defined as mandatory for that message but is syntactically incorrect (e.g., the IE content violates the coding/length rules specified for it), the UE shall diagnose this as a 'mandatory IE error'. Unless a specific abnormal-case handling is defined elsewhere in the specification for that message, the UE shall not act on the message; the UE shall discard the message and, where applicable, may return a 5GMM STATUS message with 5GMM cause value #96 'invalid mandatory information', identifying the message in which the error was detected. This ensures that messages with corrupted or malformed mandatory content are not processed as if they were valid, while allowing the network/UE peer to be informed of the error condition.

results.question: How does clause 7.5 specify the UE should handle a missing mandatory information element in a received 5GMM message?

options.A: Use a pre-configured default value for the missing element
options.B: Treat it as a protocol error and initiate appropriate error procedures
options.C: Process the message without the missing element
options.D: Request retransmission of the complete message from the network

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 7.5, Non-semantical mandatory information element errors
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 7.5 (Handling of syntactically incorrect messages / missing mandatory information elements): 'If a 5GMM message is received in which a mandatory information element is missing, the UE shall diagnose this as a syntactically incorrect message and shall apply the following: except for the messages and situations described in subclause 7.6 (extra information elements) and the message-specific abnormal case handling defined elsewhere in this specification, the UE shall discard the message. If the message needs to be acted upon, the UE shall take the actions specified for the corresponding procedure in the abnormal case (e.g., treat the request as if it had not been received, or remain in the current state). Where the specific procedure does not define an action for this situation, the UE may return a 5GMM STATUS message with 5GMM cause #96 "invalid mandatory information" and shall discard the message.'

results.question: According to clause 7.5, which of the following scenarios would NOT cause the UE to treat a 5GMM message as containing a protocol error?

options.A: Receiving a mandatory information element with incorrect syntax
options.B: Receiving a mandatory information element with correct syntax but incorrect semantics
options.C: Missing a mandatory information element in the message
options.D: Receiving an information element in an incorrect order within the message

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 7.5, Non-semantical mandatory information element errors
results.evidence: According to 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 7.5.1.2.2 (and related sub-clauses under 7.5 'Handling of unknown, unforeseen, and erroneous protocol data'), the UE shall diagnose a protocol error for conditions such as: (a) a message too short to contain a complete mandatory IE, (b) an unknown or unforeseen message type, (c) a message not compatible with the current protocol state, (d) a missing mandatory IE, (e) an IE encoded with 'comprehension required' that is unknown or unforeseen, (f) an out-of-sequence IE, and (g) a repeated IE. However, receipt of a 5GMM message containing a non-comprehension-required (optional) IE that is unknown, unforeseen, or not applicable to the message does NOT cause the UE to treat the message as containing a protocol error — such an IE is simply ignored, and the rest of the message is processed normally.

results.evidence: If the UE requests traffic segregation for multiple service data flows requiring different QoS handling, the SMF shall map each service data flow to a separate QoS flow, i.e. the SMF shall not multiplex service data flows with different QoS handling requirements onto the same QoS flow, and shall establish or modify PDU session resources accordingly by assigning distinct QoS flow identifiers (QFIs) and associated QoS rules and QoS profiles for each requested traffic segregation.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.19, Emergency number list
results.evidence: The Emergency number list IE, when received by the UE, indicates the emergency numbers that are provided by the network and that the UE shall store and use, replacing any previously stored list, for the purpose of emergency call identification. Each emergency number in the list is associated with an emergency service category value, and the UE shall use this list to determine whether a particular dialled number is to be treated as an emergency call, in addition to any UE-embedded emergency number list. The absence of an emergency number in this list does not necessarily mean it is not an emergency number if it is otherwise known to the UE (e.g., default codes such as 112 and 911, or numbers stored on the USIM). The network provides the Emergency number list IE to inform the UE of additional emergency numbers that may not be known to it by other means, so that emergency calls to these numbers can be correctly identified and handled as emergency sessions rather than normal calls.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.19, Emergency number list
results.evidence: The Emergency number list IE, as specified in clause 8.2.7.19, contains one or more emergency numbers together with associated service category information. The numbers listed in this IE are considered valid only within the PLMN (or the country of that PLMN) that provided them to the UE via the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message. In other words, the network that sends the Emergency number list IE guarantees the validity of the emergency numbers only for its own serving area (PLMN/country); the UE shall not assume these numbers remain valid if it moves to a different PLMN or country, unless that PLMN provides its own emergency number list or the UE falls back to using default/hardcoded emergency numbers.

results.question: Under what condition is the Extended protocol configuration options IE included in a message according to TS 24.501 clause 8.3.3.5?

results.question: What type of information does the Extended protocol configuration options IE carry when included by the network per TS 24.501 clause 8.3.3.5?

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.3.5, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The extended protocol configuration options IE is used to: a) transfer external network protocol options associated with a PDU session establishment; and b) transfer additional (protocol) data (e.g. configuration, error, or status information) which the network or the UE wishes to send. When included by the network, the extended protocol configuration options IE carries information such as DNS server IPv4/IPv6 addresses, P-CSCF IPv4/IPv6 addresses, IM CN subsystem signalling flag, DHCP server address, P-CSCF re-selection support, MTU size for the PDU session, and other configuration parameters that are transparently transferred between the UE and the network in support of external PDN connectivity and application-layer configuration.

results.question: Which of the following is an example of data that could be transmitted using the Extended protocol configuration options IE as described in TS 24.501 clause 8.3.3.5?

options.A: User plane data packets

options.C: Configuration parameters or messages/events
options.D: Billing and charging records

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.3.5, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The Extended protocol configuration options IE is used to transfer external network protocol options associated with a PDU session establishment or other information that needs to be passed transparently to a PDU session's external network entities, such as P-CSCF addresses for IMS, DNS server addresses, or other configuration information relevant to protocols such as PCSCF, DNS server IPv4/IPv6 address list, MTU size, etc. For example, P-CSCF IPv6 Address information (used for IMS configuration) is an example of data that could be transmitted using the Extended protocol configuration options IE.

results.question: According to TS 24.501 Clause 8.3.7.9, under what condition is the Extended protocol configuration options IE included in a message?

results.evidence: The extended protocol configuration options IE is included in the message if the UE needs to transfer protocol configuration options and their length exceeds the maximum value that can be encoded in the protocol configuration options IE (i.e. when the total length of the contents to be transferred exceeds 253 octets), in which case the protocol configuration options IE shall not be included and the extended protocol configuration options IE shall be used instead.

results.question: What type of data does TS 24.501 Clause 8.3.7.9 specify as examples that the UE might need to transmit using the Extended protocol configuration options IE?

options.A: User application data and voice packets
options.B: Configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.7.9, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The Extended protocol configuration options IE may be used to transfer external parameters between the UE and the PDN/PDU session, e.g. DHCPv4 or DHCPv6 configuration parameters, IP address allocation via NAS signalling parameters, P-CSCF address, DNS server address, and other information related to the specific PDU session or PDN connection that the UE might need to send to the network (e.g. via a MODIFY PDP CONTEXT REQUEST message, PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message, or PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message), such as data used for policy control, MS support of network requested bearer control indicator, DNS server addresses, P-CSCF addresses, additional parameters, or link MTU size information.

options.B: The UE when it has protocol data to transmit

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.7.9, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The SMF shall include this IE if the extended protocol configuration options need to be sent to the UE, e.g., in relation to LADN, DNS server addresses, P-CSCF discovery, or other DN-related information as specified in 3GPP TS 24.008 and 3GPP TS 29.061.

results.question: Under what condition is the Extended protocol configuration options IE included in a message according to TS 24.501 clause 8.3.1.9?

options.A: When the network needs to transmit protocol data to the UE
options.B: When the UE needs to transmit protocol data to the network
options.C: When the message requires additional security parameters
options.D: When the session management procedure is initiated by the network

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.1.9, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The Extended protocol configuration options IE is included in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT message when the network wants to transfer information related to a particular protocol (e.g., protocol configuration options for higher layer protocols, application-specific parameters, or DNS server addresses) that cannot be conveyed using the other information elements defined for this message.

results.question: What type of information does the Extended protocol configuration options IE enable the UE to transmit to the network, as specified in clause 8.3.1.9?

options.A: Only error codes
options.B: Only configuration parameters
options.C: Protocol data such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events
options.D: Exclusively session management messages

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.1.9, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The Extended protocol configuration options IE is used to transfer external network protocol options associated with a PDU session establishment or with a PDU session modification, and to transfer additional information depending on how it is used, such as configuration protocols and non-IP data, between the UE and the network, in a format that allows the transfer of information exceeding the length limitations of the Protocol configuration options IE.

results.question: When a UE receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message for a PDU session that is in the PDU SESSION INACTIVE state, what action must the UE take?

results.evidence: TS 24.501 §6.3.3.4 (Network-requested PDU session modification procedure – Abnormal cases in the UE): If the UE receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message for a PDU session that is in the PDU SESSION INACTIVE state, the UE shall not process the message and shall silently discard it (i.e., it shall not take any of the actions specified for the network-requested PDU session modification procedure).

options.B: Continue both procedures in parallel for the same PDU session
options.C: Abort its own procedure, enter PDU SESSION ACTIVE state, and proceed with the network's procedure
options.D: Ignore the network command and complete its own modification procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.evidence: If the UE receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message for the same PDU session with PTI value set to 'No procedure transaction identity assigned', the UE shall abort the UE-requested PDU session modification procedure and shall progress the network-requested PDU session modification procedure.

results.question: In a collision scenario between UE-requested and network-requested PDU session modification procedures, what is the required state transition for the UE before proceeding with the network's procedure?

options.A: Remain in PDU SESSION MODIFICATION PENDING
options.B: Enter PDU SESSION INACTIVE
options.C: Enter PDU SESSION ACTIVE
options.D: Enter PDU SESSION RELEASING

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.evidence: If a UE-requested PDU session modification procedure and a network-requested PDU session modification procedure collide, the network-requested PDU session modification procedure shall be progressed and the UE-requested PDU session modification procedure shall be aborted. The UE shall move the corresponding PDU session to the state PDU SESSION MODIFICATION PENDING before proceeding with the network-requested PDU session modification procedure.

results.question: In the abnormal case where a UE initiates a de-registration procedure (not due to switch off) in a cell belonging to an SNPN with a globally-unique SNPN identity for which the UE has no valid subscription, what action shall the network take according to TS 24.501 clause 5.5.2.2.7?

results.evidence: If the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message is received by the network from a cell belonging to an SNPN with a globally-unique SNPN identity for which the UE does not hold a valid subscription, the network shall not process the message any further and shall locally release any existing signalling connection with the UE.
